clue.text: Despicable driver on right side of double bend

indicators.note: the driver is placed to the right of, so after, the bend's letter

parts.note: an S is the shape of a double bend in a road, as on warning signs
a cabby is a taxi driver

explanation.surface: A motorist taking a winding road keeps to the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabby is an informal word for contemptible or mean, a synonym of despicable.

clue.text: Quack in disgrace, having handed out drug

indicators.note: something handed out is given away, so the drug's letter leaves the word for disgrace

parts.note: shame is dishonour or disgrace
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fake doctor is disgraced after dispensing narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a fraud or impostor, and a sham is likewise a pretender or fake.

clue.text: English saint, one going to a place that values Wisdom

parts.note: St Alban is honoured as the first English martyr
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An English saint travels to somewhere that prizes wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisdom is the comedian Norman Wisdom, whose films were hugely popular in communist Albania, where he remained a national favourite; the capital W is the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan country famously adored the British comic actor Norman Wisdom, so it is a country that prizes him.

clue.text: Clue with answer "teats" could show this!

definitions.text: Clue with answer "teats" could show this!

parts.note: the word is a jumbled version of a word for flavour, as an anagram clue with a bad indicator would make it

explanation.surface: A setter jokes that a clue answered by a rude word would be vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, BAD is an anagram indicator on TASTE, giving TEATS; and a clue with that answer would itself be thought vulgar, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad taste is crudeness or vulgarity, which a clue leading to a word for nipples might be accused of showing.

clue.text: Fortune-tellers, the last coming almost to the fore being David?

indicators.text: the last coming almost to the fore
indicators.note: the final letter travels nearly to the front, stopping just behind the first letter

parts.note: palmists tell fortunes by reading hands

explanation.surface: Fortune-tellers predict that the last shall be first, as in the biblical saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S moves up to second place, just short of the front. King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally held to be the author of the Psalms, making him the best-known writer of sacred songs.

clue.text: Possibly decrease mph shortly before a ____ ?

definitions.text: Possibly decrease mph shortly before a ____ ?

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might become something else, an arrangement into new order
cut short, the abbreviation loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Advice to motorists to slow down when approaching a roadside device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims MPH to MP; DECREASE plus MP rearranged gives SPEEDCAMER, then A is added. The whole clue also describes what drivers do near the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers typically brake in front of a roadside camera that photographs vehicles going too fast.

clue.text: See genuine company trying to promote women's self-worth!

definitions.text: company trying to promote women's self-worth

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
real means genuine

explanation.surface: Here is a real firm working to boost women's confidence!
explanation.walkthrough: The cosmetics firm's slogan is 'Because you're worth it', hence the self-worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cosmetics firm's long-running advertising slogan tells women they are worth it.

clue.text: Operating properly as a monk

definitions.meaning: something working correctly is functioning as it should
a monk belongs to a religious order, so he is within one

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both functioning correctly and belonging to a religious community such as the Benedictines.

clue.text: Line up correct drink for tongue-tied don?

indicators.note: the Oxford don William Spooner was famous for swapping the starts of words

parts.note: right means correct
to tope is to drink, especially heavily

explanation.surface: Fetching the proper drink for an academic who is lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial R and T of RIGHT TOPE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a taut line strung high up for performers to walk along.

clue.text: Music? Oh dreadful sounds!

indicators.note: sounds says these words are heard, standing for something spelt differently

parts.note: Oh is the exclamation and dreadful means bad, making the phrase O BAD

explanation.surface: A listener groans at how awful some music sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a piece of music or a poem greeting the dawn, so it is a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Pine endlessly, be desperate throughout an astronomical revolution

indicators.note: with no end, the word for pining loses its final letter

parts.note: to yearn is to pine
to long is to be desperate for something

explanation.surface: Someone pines without end, utterly desperate for the whole course of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting a year means continuing through one orbit of the Earth round the Sun.

clue.text: Abominated nerd playing something in the amusement arcade

indicators.note: playing suggests letters frolicking about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hated geek is gaming in an amusement arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine with a single lever arm, found in arcades, is nicknamed for robbing its players.

clue.text: Famous travellers (about 100 possibly) in mathematical array

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men who journeyed to Bethlehem
C is short for circa, Latin for about
100 is ten times ten, an example of a square number

explanation.surface: The Magi, a hundred of them perhaps, set out in a mathematical formation.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic square is a grid of numbers whose rows, columns and diagonals all sum to the same total.

clue.text: It may help someone see a giant's terribly dull

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is used as a letter here
mat is a variant of matt, meaning dull or not glossy

explanation.surface: A giant is awfully dull, says someone unkindly.
explanation.definitionFit: An anastigmat is a lens corrected for astigmatism, used to improve vision or imaging.

clue.text: A tip for the traditional hunter?

definitions.text: A tip for the traditional hunter?

parts.words: A tip for the traditional hunter?
parts.note: reads as a piece of advice for an old-style hunter, but means the pointed end of a weapon such a hunter would shoot

explanation.surface: Some advice offered to an old-fashioned huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed head of a shaft fired from a bow was the business end of the old hunter's weapon.

clue.text: Ship's goods about to be unloaded

indicators.note: unloading takes something off, so the letter for about leaves the word for goods

parts.note: cargo is goods carried by a ship
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A vessel's freight is about to be taken ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Ollie's friend Bob gets a carriage

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the comedy partner of Oliver Hardy
Bob Hope was the American comedian

explanation.surface: Oliver Hardy's sidekick gets hold of a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light, open, one-seat horse-drawn carriage named after its first builder.

clue.text: Grumble not good — a bit indecent

indicators.note: not drops the letter for good from the grumble

parts.note: a gripe is a grumble

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is rather rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe can describe language or humour that is coarse or slightly smutty.

clue.text: Friend might, in extremis, work computer

parts.note: pal means friend

indicators.note: the Latin phrase is read as just the extreme letters, the first and last

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A friend in desperate straits might get a computer working.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmtop is a small handheld computer that fits in the hand.

clue.text: Cold mushroom will be included in a supply of food, OK?

indicators.note: the pieces are taken inside the other phrase

parts.note: table means food provided, as in keeping a good table
C is short for cold, as on taps
a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Will a cold mushroom in the food be all right?
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable means satisfactory or all right, the sense of OK.

clue.text: Something to see in kitchen book — must go to library?

parts.note: a library is something that lends books

explanation.surface: A kitchen book has to be returned to the library.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is an electrical appliance for mixing food, found in kitchens.

clue.text: Old coin with the north country queen's inscription

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
coins of Queen Anne were inscribed ANNE R, for Anna Regina

explanation.surface: An old coin bears a queen's lettering from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A TANNER was the old British sixpence, in use until decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanner was the familiar British slang name for the old sixpenny coin.

clue.text: A clan quite lewd with characters disposed to be familiar

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, disposed in another order

explanation.surface: A rather bawdy clan with odd personalities is up to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-acquainted with something means knowing it well, being familiar with it.

clue.text: Finish recording informal talk in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so this is what the word sounds like

parts.note: a rap is an informal chat or talk

explanation.surface: Finishing off a session with a chat for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a wrap' is said by film directors when shooting is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: In film and recording, wrap means to finish a session or shoot.

clue.text: Language of society internalised by public schoolboy

indicators.note: taken inside, the society letter goes into the schoolboy

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A public schoolboy takes in the language of high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonian is the Finno-Ugric language spoken in Estonia, on the Baltic.

clue.text: Bird using trick to get dung beetle

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a dor is a kind of dung beetle

explanation.surface: A bird uses a trick to catch an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The condor is a huge South American vulture, one of the largest flying birds.

clue.text: In the course of act character expired

indicators.note: during something means within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
a part is a character in a play

explanation.surface: An actor's role died during one act of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is a euphemism for having died, the sense of expired.

clue.text: Listener in alehouse about to handle difficult situation?

indicators.note: in places the listener inside the other piece
about turns the word for alehouse round

parts.note: a pub is an alehouse
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone listening in a pub is about to cope with trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to stay strong and cope bravely when things are hard.
